hero.heading: Sanatana Dharma Explained
hero.description: Sanatana Dharma is the ancient spiritual philosophy of India that explains life, purpose, karma, and liberation. Discover its teachings through the Vedas, Upanishads, and Bhagavad Gita in a simple and practical way.

sections.title: What is Sanatana Dharma?
sections.content: Sanatana Dharma means the eternal way of life. It is a spiritual philosophy that teaches how to live with truth, purpose, and harmony. It is based on universal principles like dharma (duty), karma (action), and moksha (liberation). Unlike organized religions, Sanatana Dharma is a timeless system of knowledge that adapts to all people and cultures.

sections.title: Sanatana Dharma Explained in Simple Terms
sections.content: Sanatana Dharma teaches that every action has consequences (karma), every person has a duty (dharma), and the ultimate goal of life is freedom from suffering (moksha). It encourages self-realization, compassion, and balance between material and spiritual life.

items.title: Dharma (Duty)
items.description: Living with righteousness, responsibility, and moral values.

items.title: Karma (Action)
items.description: Every action has consequences that shape your life.

items.title: Moksha (Liberation)
items.description: Freedom from the cycle of birth and rebirth.

items.title: Ahimsa (Non-violence)
items.description: Respect and compassion for all living beings.

sections.title: Main Scriptures of Sanatana Dharma
sections.content: The teachings of Sanatana Dharma come from ancient scriptures that explain philosophy, ethics, and spirituality in depth.

items.title: Vedas
items.description: The oldest spiritual texts containing knowledge about the universe, rituals, and truth.

items.title: Upanishads
items.description: Philosophical teachings about the soul (Atman) and ultimate reality (Brahman).

items.title: Bhagavad Gita
items.description: A practical guide to life, duty, and spiritual growth through the dialogue of Krishna and Arjuna.

items.title: Ramayana & Mahabharata
items.description: Epic stories that teach dharma, devotion, and moral values.

sections.title: Why Sanatana Dharma Matters Today
sections.content: In today’s fast-paced world, Sanatana Dharma provides clarity, mental peace, and purpose. Its teachings help people manage stress, make ethical decisions, and live a balanced life. It promotes mindfulness, sustainability, and harmony with nature.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Sanatana Dharma and Hinduism?
faqs.answer: Sanatana Dharma is the original eternal philosophy, while Hinduism is a modern term used to describe related traditions.

faqs.question: Is Sanatana Dharma a religion?
faqs.answer: It is more than a religion. It is a way of life and a philosophical system guiding human existence.

faqs.question: What is the goal of life in Sanatana Dharma?
faqs.answer: The ultimate goal is moksha, or liberation from the cycle of birth and rebirth.

home.ourfourcoreyugassubtitle: The eternal and universal way of life based on truth, righteousness, and spiritual principles that uphold cosmic order. These numbers are not random. They are derived from a base unit of 432,000, multiplied proportionally (4: 3: 2: 1). One Full Day of Brahma: Lifetime of Brahma - 100 Brahma years - Each year = 360 days - Each day = 4 yugas (ages) - Total = 311,040,000,000 human years.
